title: Group employment tribunal claims
readYourLetter: Read your letter from the tribunal for the reasons why the tribunal thinks your claim should be joint with others.
contentsLink2: If the tribunal added you to an existing group of claims
contentsLink3: If you or someone else submitted a claim for you and others
whatIsGroupClaimP1: A group claim is when more than one claimant's claims are managed together, and are sometimes dealt with at the same hearing. This is because they share legal or factual issues, or they are similar claims against the same employer or organization.
whatIsGroupClaimInsetText: You may have submitted a group claim with other people, or the tribunal added your claim to another group claim.
whatIsGroupClaimP2: Group claims can help parties and the tribunal deal with similar claims more efficiently.
whatIsGroupClaimP3: Group claim parties can still try to agree a settlement before the tribunal gives a judgment. This can be directly between parties, or through mediation services provided by Acas.
whatIsGroupClaimP4: The tribunal will tell you who should attend the hearing and what to expect.
addedToGroupHeading: If the tribunal added you to another group of claims
addedToGroupP1: If the tribunal thinks your claim should be joined with others, you have the right to object. If you do not object, you do not need to do anything.
addedToGroupP2: The tribunal will contact you and tell you how to respond, and if there are time limits to respond if you have any objections. This will be posted or emailed to you.
addedToGroupP3: The outcome of your individual claim will not be affected if the tribunal agrees to keep your claim separate from others.
madeGroupClaimHeading: If you or someone else made the group claim for you and others
madeGroupClaimP1: The person who submitted the claim on behalf of others may be referred to as the group representative. This is different to a professional legal representative.
asGroupRepP1: They may not need to represent all the other claims, but the tribunal will tell them what they need to do.
asGroupRepP2: As the group representative, it is their responsibility to:
asGroupRepBullet1: be the single point of contact for the tribunal
asGroupRepBullet2: update the other claimants about hearings and any directions from the tribunal
asGroupRepP3: The group representative does not have access to anyone's personal claim details. In some cases, they may need to ask other claimants for information.
notGroupRepHeading: If you are in a group claim but not the group representative
notGroupRepP1: If you are not the group representative you may not need to do anything unless the tribunal asks you to provide something. You can still contact other claimants in your group claim, but any contact with the tribunal should be done by your representative.
notGroupRepP2: Contact details of the other claimants is in the 'Schedule' document. You can see this output for the Schedule document.
notGroupRepInsetText: Other claimants in your group claim can see your name, but not the details of your ET1 claim.
legalRepAddedSubHeading: When the tribunal has added you to another group of claims
legalRepAddedP1: You might not know the other claimants and they may have one or more legal representatives already. You do not need one, but you can still name your own legal representative. The tribunal will tell you if there is a legal representative already in the group claim. You can ask them if they'll represent you too.
legalRepMadeSubHeading: When you or someone else made the group claim for you and others
legalRepMadeP1: Any claimant in a group claim can have a legal representative. As a group, you can decide if you want a legal representative to represent the group. This can reduce costs for all parties, compared to individual group members having their own representative.
legalRepGuidanceLinkText: See our guidance on hiring a legal representative.
leavingP1: If you are in a group claim, you can ask to be removed and have your claim treated separately. You will need to ask the tribunal, who will tell you how to do this. You must explain why your claim should be heard separately.
leavingP2: If you want to end your individual claim completely, you must tell the tribunal through your online account. If you withdraw your individual claim, you will no longer be part of the group claim.
howToUseOnlineAccountHeading: How to use your online account
howToUseOnlineAccountP1: Your case overview will show that your claim is now in a group of claims.
howToUseOnlineAccountP2: You can make an application or contact the tribunal to ask or tell it something from your case overview.
howToUseOnlineAccountP3: You can view communication from other parties in 'Group claim requests and applications' from your case overview. You may be able to respond to applications and requests made by other parties if the judge has not decided on them yet.
howToUseOnlineAccountP4: The tribunal will email you with any updates to the group claim, and these will be visible in your online account.
